page: Amazon Web Services m7a.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by 4th generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running on the AWS Nitro System. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 vCPU-to-core mapping operating at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is paired with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory rated at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio across its 8 vCPUs. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware benchmark testing highlights particularly strong single-core compute capabilities. The instance scores in the top 25% of evaluated cloud servers on stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core evaluations. Multi-threaded throughput, as measured by multi-core stress-ng and PassMark CPU suites, aligns with median expectations for an 8-core configuration. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers 39.62 GB/sec read and 27.38 GB/sec write bandwidth on large blocks, driving solid throughput in memory-sensitive tasks such as Redis in-memory operations and static web delivery.

The m7a.2xlarge does not include dedicated graphics accelerators or bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent storage relies on external network-attached volumes. Networking baseline performance is provisioned at 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. The absence of hyperthreading eliminates thread contention across workloads, offering consistent per-core execution times and strong latency predictability.

This server offers solid cost efficiency for mid-tier workloads requiring dedicated compute resources, modern AVX-512 extensions, and rapid single-threaded processing without incurring the cost of higher-density memory tiers or specialized accelerators. Primary operational fits include mid-sized relational database hosting, containerized microservices, build and CI/CD pipelines, static web serving, and small-model CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an 8-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz and built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Operating with dedicated physical cores and no simultaneous multithreading, it delivers 8 vCPUs alongside 32.0 GB of DDR5 system memory at 5 GHz. Instruction support includes AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions. Benchmark results demonstrate top-quartile single-core CPU execution, single-threaded decompression speeds, and strong text processing, with overall multi-core and memory bandwidth matching median expectations. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps and lacks local ephemeral storage or integrated GPU hardware. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio, the m7a.2xlarge is well-proportioned for mid-tier application hosting, continuous integration runners, relational databases, and lightweight CPU-based language model inference.
